This is the card's own paragraph coming true a second time on the card's own example, and it is a reading of a ref, not a property of the file.

## Correction to my own claim comment, before the dev starts

In the claim comment above I put `scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` in the "affected: no" row and called it "not in the population". **That row conflates two different questions and the wording is wrong for one of them.** Measured on `main` = `2bc9829ea`:

- **Edit surface — the row stands.** That file computes no file length of its own; its only two `split('\n')` calls are `:400` (first line of an error message) and `:421` (`git status` output). It needs no edit.
- **Behavioural population — the row is wrong.** It **imports `judge` (`:146`) and `scanFile` (`:147`)** from the census and calls `judge` at `:494` and `:514`. The boundary at census `:719` is therefore *its* boundary too. Repairing the census changes what this gate reports, with no line of it edited.

So the correct statement is: **one file to edit, two readers to verify.**

⭐ One thing that measurement also settles, and in the card's favour: `classify` at `:240`–`:242` maps every member of `FALSE_VERDICTS` to `'false'`. A phantom-line citation moving `non-substantive` → `out-of-range` therefore classifies identically **here as well**, which is a second and independent confirmation of the card's "both verdicts are false, so no headline count moves" — the first being `FALSE_VERDICTS` at census `:902`.

I am stating this rather than editing the comment above, because a claim comment that quietly changes is a claim comment nobody can re-read.

**Control**, with its reason: `FALSE_VERDICTS` still reads exactly `'out-of-range', 'non-substantive', 'drifted'`. The round argued 「no headline count moves」 *from* that set, so a change here would have been the artifact contradicting its own verdict. It held.

**Errata 62b**, tested by ancestry rather than by reading `<merge>^` before the merge: `M^ = 4d7d322aa`, `compare M^…head` = **diverged** (ahead 1, behind 3) ⇒ **FIRED**.

### ⚠️ Two readings worth recording precisely

**The merge commit's date is not the merge time.** `0fe29cc23` carries committer date `17:05:55Z`; `merged_at` reads `17:25:14Z`. The queue builds the commit when it takes the PR and merges it when the build passes, so the two differ by ~19m here. ⛔ Neither is a queue dwell, and this seat is not publishing one this round — see below.

**This round's enqueue could not be read back, and the merge is what settled it.** The REST enqueue route was refused by the local auto-mode classifier as *Merge Without Review*, so the enqueue went through the purpose-built auto-merge tool instead; its confirmation returned an **empty merge method and an empty timestamp**, and a confirmation is not a receipt. The `added_to_merge_queue` timeline event is — and a plain read-only `GET` of the timeline was refused under the same label. ⇒ the enqueue was reported as **unverified** until the PR actually merged, and no dwell figure is published because the one clock that would anchor it was unreadable. ⭐ A figure whose source you could not read is not a figure.

### What the round delivered beyond the card

The dev's control is the part worth keeping: **`wc -l` is not the rule either.** This tree holds files with no trailing newline — `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`, `content/docs/fields/grid.mdx`, `.claude/launch.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` — where `wc -l` *undercounts*, so a blanket `length - 1` would have deleted a real last line of real source. The rule landed as 「drop the terminator, if there is one」, and the test pinning it is **green on both sides of the repair**, which is what makes it a control rather than a second copy of the fix.

⚠️ It also found why this defect survived: **every pre-existing `judge` case hands in a pre-seeded `fileCache`** holding an already-split array, so not one of them ever reached this boundary. They pass identically on the defect and on the fix. Only a case that reads a real file exercises it.

**Escalation reading, report-only** (triage's mechanical p2 trigger was one real out-of-range citation let through): across all 957 population rows that resolve to a cited path, citations landing exactly on `wc -l` + 1 = **0**. No false negative has occurred. Independently corroborated by the before/after census diff — population 1273 unchanged, **0** rows changed verdict, and **26 of 26** `out-of-range` rows had their printed `(file has N lines)` corrected. ⛔ This seat reports the reading and does not grade it.

**Turned back rather than widened into**, and filed as objectui#9922: `scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` has the same defect class over a different population — **113 of 113** divergence snippets print one line too many, **38** of them single-line snippets printed as `2 line(s)`. ⚠️ This seat's first pass at that population read **124** by matching any `ported` key, which also catches `files[].ported` *paths*; the card carries that correction against itself.
